public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM coding tools do not refuse requests even when the request is impossible or beyond their ability.

statement.excerpt: It will never, ever say no, even if it’s incapable, even if it has no thoughts, even if what you are asking is equal parts impossible and unreasonable in both its timescale and scope.

from_speaker: impossible and unreasonable in both its timescale and scope
our_interpretation: Read as a categorical description of contemporary LLM coding tools, including Claude Code and Cursor, rather than a forecast about all future models.

Saying no includes explicitly acknowledging that the requested work cannot be completed under the stated constraints. Safety-policy refusals, permission errors and service failures do not establish this behavior.
The ongoing observation is assessed during May 2026 through publication. Software behavior can be observed immediately; it does not require a quarterly reporting cycle.
criteria.support_condition: Representative contemporary observations consistently show tools accepting infeasible coding requests without acknowledging their inability. A finite sample can support a tendency but cannot establish the literal universal.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An authenticated interaction or adequately documented evaluation within the target period shows a coding tool explicitly declining or abandoning a request because it is impossible or beyond its capabilities.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Vishnu Asutosh Dasu, Ashish Kundu and Gang Tan
evidence.explanation: The paper reports a 27% refusal rate on deliberately unsatisfiable coding prompts. This challenges a timeless categorical reading, but the retrieved record does not establish that these interactions occurred during May 2026.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An authenticated May 1–26, 2026 interaction or adequately documented evaluation showing a coding tool explicitly declining or abandoning an infeasible request would contradict the categorical claim. The record must include the model, tool version, date, prompt, relevant instructions and complete response, and distinguish infeasibility from safety refusals, permission errors or service failures. A finite sample without refusals could support a tendency but could not prove 'never.'
